chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from 'Ali from Abu Basir said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the divorce of a female slave, and he said, 'Two divorces.' And he said, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'The waiting period of the female slave whose husband dies is two months and five days, and the waiting period of the divorced female slave is one month and a half.'
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a female slave in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the distinct 'iddah periods for a female slave (ama), differentiating between the two-and-a-half months required upon her husband's death and the one-and-a-half months mandated for divorce. This ruling highlights the jurisprudential nuance in Shia fiqh where the status of slavery modifies the standard waiting periods applied to free women, reflecting the socio-legal context of early Islamic society.
